author: reek
body: Adversarial probe for the board HAL. Driving a GPIO register is device I/O, so a function that does it cannot be typed pure. Before the HAL carried honest effect rows this compiled clean: Board.codex's MMIO primitives were typed Integer -> Integer, so every register access in the board layer was invisible to the effect system, to the capability manifest, and to the boot grant -- while the chapter's own prose claimed the type system enforced exactly this.

author: reek
body: The sanctioned form is hal-device-declared: declare [Device.Mmio] and the same code type-checks. The effect is real and declarable, not a blanket ban.

author: reek
body: The Boards quire is effect-exempt (a driver is expected to do I/O), so this is about application and library code reaching past the drivers to the registers directly.
